sense: of the past: I used to play

terms.gloss: I used to play, I used to see
evidence: Aug. Conf. 1.9.15: quia lūdēbam pilā puer
terms.comment: The imperfect alone says what went on, or was done again and again, in the past; saepe, ōlim or puer (as a boy) make the habit plain.

terms.gloss: be in the habit of; in the imperfect, used to
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation, semi-deponent, with an infinitive
evidence: Ov. Ars 2.341: quem taurum metuis, vitulum mulcēre solēbās
Mart. 13.14.1: clūdere quae cēnās lactūca solēbat avōrum
terms.comment: Names the habit outright; for the present, see usually. “Be used to” (accustomed) is another verb: adsuēscō (assuēscō), as Milo vitulum adsuēverat ferre, had got used to carrying the calf (Quint. 1.9.5).

phrases.english: because as a boy I used to play ball

phrases.latin: C. Duellium … redeuntem ā cēnā senem saepe vidēbam puer
phrases.english: as a boy I often used to see old Gaius Duilius coming home from dinner

phrases.latin: quem taurum metuis, vitulum mulcēre solēbās
phrases.english: the bull you are afraid of, you used to stroke when it was a calf

phrases.latin: clūdere quae cēnās lactūca solēbat avōrum, dīc mihi, cūr nostrās inchoat illa dapēs?
phrases.english: Lettuce used to close our grandfathers’ dinners: tell me, why does it open ours?

phrases.latin: ut Milō, quem vitulum adsuēverat ferre, taurum ferēbat
phrases.english: as Milo carried as a bull the animal he had got used to carrying as a calf
